title: Graphical FTC with a lower limit inside the interval

stimulus.title: The graph of $f$ on $[-2, 6]$
stimulus.text: The continuous function $f$ is defined on $[-2, 6]$. Its graph is a semicircle of radius 2 above the x-axis from $x = -2$ to $x = 2$, a segment from $(2, 0)$ to $(4, -2)$, and a segment from $(4, -2)$ to $(6, 2)$. Let $g(x) = \int_2^x f(t)\,dt$ for $-2 \le x \le 6$.

plot.label: Graph of f on [-2, 6]: an upper semicircle of radius 2 centered at the origin from -2 to 2, a segment from (2, 0) to (4, -2), and a segment from (4, -2) to (6, 2)

accept: the quarter disc of area pi taken with a negative sign

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the absolute minimum value of $g$ on the closed interval $[-2, 6]$. Justify your answer.

rubric.point: Identifies the critical points from $g'(x) = f(x)$: $x = 2$ and $x = 5$ (where $f$ changes sign)

accept: a table of the four values

rubric.point: Answer: the absolute minimum value is $-2\pi$, at $x = -2$

parts.sample: $g'(x) = f(x) = 0$ at $x = 2$ and $x = 5$ in $(-2, 6)$. Candidates: $g(-2) = -\int_{-2}^2 f(t)\,dt = -2\pi$, $g(2) = 0$, $g(5) = -2 - 1 = -3$, $g(6) = -2$. The least value is $-2\pi \approx -6.28$, so the absolute minimum of $g$ on $[-2, 6]$ is $-2\pi$, at $x = -2$.

parts.label: c
parts.sample: By the Fundamental Theorem and the chain rule, $k'(x) = f(3x) \cdot 3$. So $k'(1) = 3f(3) = 3(-1) = -3$.

parts.label: d
parts.sample: This is a limit of right Riemann sums with $\Delta x = \frac{4}{n}$ and $x_i = -2 + \frac{4i}{n}$ on $[-2, 2]$, so it equals $\int_{-2}^{2} f(x)\,dx$, the area of the half-disc of radius 2: $\frac{1}{2}\pi(2)^2 = 2\pi$.
